text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- On the 78th anniversary of the first proclamation of Latvia's independence, parliament speaker Alfred Chepanis adressed President Guntis Ulmanis, Prime Minister Andris Shkele deputies and the diplomatic corps. He focussed on issues concerning relations between parliament and government and stressed the need for cooperation between both institutions.
- A concert dedicated to this occasion was held in the National Theatre where in 1918 independence was declared.

- The congress of the right-wing radical People's Movement 'For Latvia' was held in Jelgava, about 40 km from Riga. Party leader Joachim Siegerist, a German who has one Latvian parent, surprised with his first speech in Latvian as he is known not to be able to speak the language.

- The state audit office issued a statement that only 47.2 percent of companies report properly on their financial activities and it has suggested fining offenders, which would bring in around 2.62 million lats to the state budget.
- Foreign ministry state secretary Maris Riekstinsh told the Lithuanian Ambassador in Latvia, Rimantas Karazijas, that Latvia will never accept Lithuania's unilateral settlement of the sea border.
- President Ulmanis met the Chief Rabbi of Riga and Latvia, Natan Barkans.

- Company LUKoil-Baltija bought for 1.72 million lats the Riga oil base in an auction organised by the Latvian Privatisation Agency. LUKoil-Baltija has to pay all the debts of the enterprise, about one million lats.
